preamble: Prothesis or epenthesis of [h] involves the insertion of a glottal fricative before a vowel-initial word or syllable. This can occur as a way to avoid hiatus. It is also seen in the historical development of Ancient Greek. A related environment is preaspiration, where [h] is inserted before a stop, as in Samic (Proto-Samic *kietë 'hand' > Northern Sami giehta).

examples.note: Word-initial υ always took the rough breathing (h), so vowel-initial *u- acquired a prothetic [h].
Preaspiration: an [h] developed before strong-grade single stops and affricates in all Samic languages except Akkala, Kildin and Ter; South Sami gïete lacks it in this word.

examples.to: Northern Sami johka, Lule Sami jåhkå, South Sami johke
examples.note: Skolt Sami jokk shows a geminate instead.
